title: Memory Visualizer
description: Watch variables, arrays, and the call stack change live as your algorithm runs -- and learn to spot memory bugs before they crash your program.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Every variable, array, and function call your algorithm makes consumes memory. Understanding those state changes is core to writing stable code.

subsections.title: Real-Time State Inspection
subsections.content: Console output only shows the final result. The Memory Visualizer shows the states in between:
bullets: The exact moment a variable is allocated.
Every value mutation, step by step.
Memory being freed when a function returns.

subsections.title: Real-Time State Tracking
subsections.content: Watch a counter increment one step at a time, see exactly what happens during a variable swap, and see an array grow as items are appended.

sections.title: Variable State Changes
sections.content: The visualizer tracks each variable's name, current value, type, and its full history of changes.

subsections.title: Tracking the Boxes
subsections.content: Step through each change to watch your algorithm's logic unfold value by value.

subsections.title: Micro-Transition: Safe Data Swapping
subsections.content: Swapping two variables without a temporary holding spot overwrites and loses data. The visualizer makes it obvious why a temp variable is required.

subsections.title: The Auxiliary Variable Concept
bullets: Save a's value into a temp variable.
Copy the temp value into b.

subsections.title: Diagnosing Data Loss
subsections.content: Skip the temp variable and the visualizer shows both variables collapsing to the same value -- pinpointing exactly where the original data was lost.

sections.title: Tracking Arrays
sections.content: Arrays hold ordered data, addressed by numeric index.

subsections.title: Index Verification
subsections.content: Index 0 is always the first element -- appending or popping automatically shifts the rest.

subsections.title: Visualizing Array Operations
bullets: Removed elements fade, and remaining indices shift automatically.

subsections.title: Identifying Boundary Violations
subsections.content: Off-by-one errors show up visually as reads/writes to indices that don't exist yet -- step through your loop to catch the exact moment it goes out of bounds.

subsections.title: Defensive Programming
subsections.content: Feed an empty array to your code and watch what happens -- accessing item 0 of an empty list crashes. Always add an "Edge Case Check" at the top of your function to catch this before it happens.

sections.title: Introduction to Memory
sections.content: Creating a list, or growing one, requests new memory for each item -- that's **O(n) space**. Updating a variable or swapping values in place changes what's already there, with no new memory needed -- that's **O(1) space**.

sections.title: Understanding the Call Stack
sections.content: Function calls are tracked with a Last-In-First-Out structure called the Call Stack.

subsections.title: Stack Frames
subsections.content: Each function call gets its own frame holding its local data. When it returns, that frame is removed and execution resumes one level up.

subsections.title: Visualizing Recursive Depth
subsections.content: A recursive countdown from 3 stacks three frames before hitting the base case and unwinding back down -- the visualizer shows each one.

subsections.title: Stack Overflow Diagnosis
subsections.content: Frames pop off in reverse order once the base case is reached. If recursion never reaches its base case, frames pile up endlessly -- that's a Stack Overflow.

subsections.title: Variable Scoping: Local vs. Global
subsections.content: Global-style variables can get overwritten by deeper recursive calls. Use local function parameters to keep each recursion level's data isolated.

sections.title: State Tracking & Rollback
sections.content: Backtracking follows a choose → explore → unchoose pattern -- whatever you add to test a path, you must remove before trying the next one.

subsections.title: The Importance of Popping
subsections.content: Append before a recursive call, then pop right after it returns. The visualizer is the fastest way to confirm your array is rolling back correctly instead of accumulating stale guesses.

sections.title: Why Memory Visualization Matters
sections.content: Most memory bugs come from misunderstanding what's actually changing during execution -- the visualizer catches them instantly.

subsections.title: Faster Debugging
subsections.content: Accidentally reset your "total" variable inside the loop instead of before it? The visualizer shows it dropping to zero every iteration -- bug spotted in seconds.

subsections.title: Professional Tools
subsections.content: Real engineers use the same idea daily:
bullets: Browser DevTools track JS variables live.
IDE debuggers (VS Code, PyCharm) have watch panels.
Memory profilers catch leaks in production servers.

subsections.title: Building Engineering Skills
subsections.content: Learning the Memory Visualizer here builds the same debugging instincts professional engineers rely on.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Memory isn't magic -- the visualizer makes every change observable.

subsections.title: The Visualizer Workflow
bullets: 3. Watch variables change to confirm your logic.
4. Check arrays after each operation for off-by-one errors.
5. Watch the Call Stack when using functions to avoid a Stack Overflow.
